title: Mashed Potato from Dry Mix with Milk and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Mashed potato from a dry mix prepared with milk and cheese is a convenient, tasty side dish. The dry mix contains dehydrated potatoes, spices, and sometimes powdered dairy components. Adding milk and grated cheese creates a creamy texture and a rich cheesy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry mixes allow quick preparation without peeling and boiling fresh potatoes.
Milk makes the mash smoother, while cheese adds a golden aroma.
These mixes are popular in military mess halls and camping rations because of their long shelf life.
Vitamin C content drops compared to fresh potatoes, but potassium and many B‑vitamins remain.
Cheese can be swapped for other dairy products like cottage cheese or Parmesan to vary the taste.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in amino‑acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: Starch‑based carbohydrates quickly convert to glucose, supplying the body with energy.

items.title: Protein from cheese
items.content: Grated cheese adds dairy protein, useful for tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Calcium from milk and cheese
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone health, teeth, and nerve transmission.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains milk and cheese, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some dry mixes include added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Additive presence
items.content: Preservatives and flavor enhancers may be present in the mix, which not everyone tolerates well.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot water or milk over the mix, stir until smooth, then fold in grated cheese and, if desired, a pat of butter. Serve hot as a side to meat or fish dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dry mix in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. Once prepared, consume the mash within 2‑3 days, storing it in the refrigerator.
